- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant noted that a specific variant of the ACTN3 gene, the R577X polymorphism, is associated with increased power and sprint performance.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant explained the PPARδ gene, which regulates lipid metabolism and energy homeostasis, and that activating it has been shown to enhance endurance.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant mentioned that activating PPARδ increases the proportion of slow-twitch muscle fibers, important for sustained, long-duration activities.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant discussed the MSTN gene, which encodes myostatin, a negative regulator of muscle growth.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant noted that inhibition or deletion of the MSTN gene can lead to increased muscle mass and strength, as observed in animals with natural mutations.
